blindSummary: This state/province is the country's main tourist corridor with a documented policing problem. The hotel zone of its largest tourism city is a massive international tourism envelope with a commercially gay-friendly surface, but municipal and state police have been repeatedly documented committing discriminatory acts against LGBT+ people, with multiple recorded assaults during detention concentrated in resort towns along the corridor; the community describes officers as untrained in human-rights standards. The municipal equality directorate recorded three formal discrimination complaints in a single year, including violence against a transgender woman, and two tourist-police officers were fired after their own body cameras showed them running an extortion ring against visitors with portable card terminals. The main tourist city's immigration detention facility is documented as a place of systematic rights violations with no accountability — relevant to a visitor whose documents are questioned. Countervailing: the state/province enacted legal gender recognition in 2020 and banned conversion practices in December 2023.
blindSourceSummaries: An international human-rights organisation feature (31 March 2025), a country-wide survey of legal gender recognition: 22 of 32 states/provinces had legislated a procedure by March 2025, while six states/provinces had reformed nothing, leaving trans people's documents permanently mismatched; also documents coercive detention and border scrutiny risks for document-mismatched travellers.

An international human-rights organisation report (6 March 2024) on trans people denied legal gender recognition in a sibling state/province: interviews with trans people about daily discrimination, harassment and differential treatment; highlights the August 2023 killing of a trans woman, found in a river with a concrete block tied to her feet; co-authored with a local community centre.

A national newspaper report (18 July 2024): the capital approved a transfeminicide-criminalisation statute — the first such offence recognised there, named for a trans woman murdered in 2016 whose case remained unpunished; adopted amid public celebration by activists.
blindLocalsOnly: The state/province's 2020 legal gender recognition procedure and its December 2023 ban on conversion practices are resident-facing; neither changes the exposure of a visitor.
